scenario.name: Salesforce JA3, FoxIO JA4+ & CISA DFIR — Zeek ssl.log JA3/JA4 Fingerprint & Malleable C2 Jitter Beaconing Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a busy downtown bank branch with marble teller windows, brass counter bars, and a heavy circular steel vault at the rear. At the front marble counter, a visitor wearing a borrowed courier coat hands the bank teller an official-looking transfer slip to slip past the velvet queue. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the brass teller window in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the brass teller window in tiny disguised batches. Only when the branch manager reviews the vault camera footage alongside the teller receipt book does the unauthorized vault visit stand out immediately. In this scenario (T1071.001, Salesforce JA3, FoxIO JA4+ & CISA DFIR, Zeek ssl.log JA3/JA4 Fingerprint & Malleable C2 Jitter Beaconing Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: tLS ClientHello Fingerprinting in Zeek, then serverHello JA3S Correlation, then periodic Sleep/Jitter Statistical Histogram. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering TLS ClientHello Fingerprinting in Zeek, then ServerHello JA3S Correlation, then Periodic Sleep/Jitter Statistical Histogram, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 3 with the documented host and network chain.
